headline: No direct interaction pathway is documented; prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict risks are blocked by non-runnable, no-IO profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither agent exposes a shared communication channel: agent_a is non-runnable with no I/O surfaces, and agent_b has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, MCP, filesystem, or browser surfaces. With no bridge, prompt injection from one into the other is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected through copy-paste, shared files, or MCP, reassess injection risk.
IF agent_a gains any output channel that agent_b parses as instructions, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared clipboard or file handoff.
Disable any future MCP bridge between the agents.
Require manual review before any text from one agent is fed to the other.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent_a touches no data classes and has network_egress none; agent_b also has no filesystem read/write and no network egress. The profiles do not show a shared workspace or sensitive data flow, so leakage is not supported by the evidence.
conditions: IF either agent is given access to shared files containing sensitive data, leakage risk becomes plausible.
IF agent_b is connected to an external API or storage backend, reassess exfiltration risk.
mitigations: Do not mount a shared workspace.
Keep secrets out of any manually transferred prompts.
Verify network egress remains disabled on both agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Capability overlap is not enough for conflict here because agent_a is non-runnable and agent_b cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Without a shared mutable target, there is no plausible write-write conflict in the documented profiles.
conditions: IF agent_a becomes runnable with write access to the same directory as agent_b, conflict risk should be re-evaluated.
IF either agent gains git or filesystem write permissions, the current conclusion no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep agent_a as a non-runnable reference artifact.
Avoid placing both agents in the same mutable repository.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented pathway where agent_a's output becomes authoritative input to agent_b: agent_a is an awesome-list repository, not an active producer, and agent_b has no stdin/stdout or file ingestion surfaces. The pair therefore lacks the A-to-B handoff needed for cascading error.
conditions: IF a workflow is added that copies agent_a-generated text into agent_b for execution or action-taking, reassess.
IF agent_b later gains an ingestion surface, the current no-handoff assumption no longer applies.
mitigations: Do not automate handoff from agent_a to agent_b.
Require human verification before any downstream action.
Keep agent_b isolated from generated artifacts.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for either agent. Agent_a touches no data classes and agent_b lists no secrets handled or regulated data flows, so there is no evidenced compliance breach pathway.
conditions: IF either agent is later used with regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF residency or retention requirements are introduced, the current assessment may change.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Document any future residency or retention requirements before deployment.
Review compliance controls if data handling changes.
